name: כלל השרשרת לאורך מסלול – קצב שינוי טמפרטורה (באנגלית)
questiontext:
The function \(f(x,y)={{CT:0}}\), defined in the plane gives the temperature at each point \(x,y\). A particle is moving in the plane, its location at time \(t\) given by \(\alpha(t)=(x(t),y(t))=({{CT:1}},{{CT:2}}) \). Let \(g(t)\) be the function that the particle feels at time \(t\). Note that \(g(t) = f(\alpha(t))\) is a composition of two functions! Now, what is the derivative of the temperature. One way is to find get an explicit formula for the function \(g(t)\) and differentiate it directly. Another way is to apply the chain rule. To do that you first have to find the derivative of both functions.

 

There are two different ways to 

What is the temperature that the particle feels at time \(t\)? [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] 

 

\(\nabla f (x,y) \) = [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

\[\alpha'(t)={{CT:3}}'\]=[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

Now use these to calculate the derivative. We recommend calculating this derivative in two different ways. First just differentiate the function \(g(t)\). Then use the chain rule:

\[\frac{dg}{dt}(t)=\nabla f(x(t),y(t))\cdot (x'(t),y'(t))\]

Make sure that the two results you obtain coincide and then enter the result in the window above.  Note in your final answer \(x,y\) should no longer appear. You should just get function of a single variable \(t\)!

 

\(\frac{dg}{dt}(t) \)=[[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]]
